answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may place jobs or claim rewards. The protocol links voting weight to that stake, not to the number of accounts, and slashes deposits for provable double-claims or conflicting attestations. Splitting funds across a mesa of aliases therefore creates no extra influence; it only multiplies setup and monitoring costs, while each alias must anchor capital that cannot wander freely until released. Attackers must tie up real value and risk losing it.
